## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Frame counters with an event log for a video pipeline.
Version: the VERSION register. NCH 32-bit counters, each advanced by a frame marker
pulse (eof_i[i], one clock; an end or a start of frame at some point of
the pipeline): in video_processor channel 0 counts the frames leaving
the first pipeline stage (csi2_raw_unpack) and channel 1 the frames
reaching the last stream stage (into axis_to_video). Every marker also
sets STATUS[i]; irq_o[i] = STATUS[i] & IRQ_EN[i] (level, until the CPU
writes 1 to STATUS[i]), so the CPU can read COUNT[i] at each end of
frame. A marker in the same clock as a CLEAR still counts (the counter
becomes 1).
Event log: every marker of a channel enabled in EV_EN is queued, in the
order the markers happened, in an EVQ-entry FIFO with its channel, the
channel's count after the marker and a timestamp (TIME, a free-running
counter advanced every TS_DIV clocks: TS_DIV = clock MHz gives
microseconds). Markers of several channels in one clock are queued
lowest channel first (same timestamp). The CPU reads the oldest entry
(EVENT, EVENT_TIME) and removes it by writing EVENT_POP; reading has no
side effect. A marker that finds the log full is lost and sets
EVENT[30] (overflow) until EVENT_POP[1] clears it.
The logic of frame_counter: its registers come and go on the cfg_* /
sts_* ports. frame_counter_top.sv is the block with its AXI4-Lite
register map (src/include/frame_counter_regs.sv: ID "FCNT" / VERSION /
DATE at 0x00-0x08, IRQ_EN 0x18, STATUS 0x1C, CLEAR 0x20, EVENT 0x24,
EVENT_TIME 0x28, EVENT_POP 0x2C, COUNT[i] 0x30 + 4 i, TIME 0x50, EV_EN
0x54).
A marker of a channel whose previous event is still pending (not yet
moved into the log) replaces it and sets the overflow. Golden model:
model/frame_counter_model.py (FrameCounterCore, clock exact; tb/python).
Clock - clk (the pipeline pixel clock). Reset - synchronous active low
rst_n.

frame_counter with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the block
designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map frame_counter_regs
(u_regs, src/include/frame_counter_regs.sv, ID "FCNT", VERSION and DATE
at 0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the logic frame_counter
(u_core, src/frame_counter.sv), joined by the register interface
frame_counter_regs_if (u_regs_if). Generated by ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py
from frame_counter_regs.json and the ports of frame_counter: regenerate
after changing either. Clock - clk. Reset - synchronous active low rst_n.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - frame_counter (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] AMD, "AXI4-Stream Video IP and System Design Guide", UG934 (2022),
//   https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/products/adaptive-socs-and-
//   fpgas/technologies/axi4-stream-video-ip-and-system-design-guide.pdf - TUSER(0) = SOF on the
//   first pixel, TLAST = EOL
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Frame markers of an AXI4-Stream video are SOF (TUSER on the first pixel) and EOL (TLAST);
//   counting frames uses one marker per frame.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: one count per marker pulse, event log with timestamps, W1C status (no algorithmic
//   standard applies).
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```

### Register map (from `frame_counter_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "FCNT" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x18 | IRQ_EN | RW | 0 | interrupt enable per channel | - |
| 0x1C | STATUS | W1C | 0 | marker seen per channel (interrupt while enabled); write 1 to clear | - |
| 0x20 | CLEAR | WO | 0 | write 1s: clear COUNT[i] | - |
| 0x24 | EVENT | RO | 0 | oldest logged event | VALID[31] an event is logged; OVERFLOW[30] events lost (log was full); CHANNEL[26:24] channel of the marker; COUNT[23:0] the channel's count after the marker |
| 0x28 | EVENT_TIME | RO | 0 | timestamp of that event (TIME ticks) | - |
| 0x2C | EVENT_POP | WO | 0 | log control | POP[0] 1: remove the oldest event; OVF_CLR[1] 1: clear the overflow flag |
| 0x30 + 4 i (i < NCH) | COUNT | RO | 0 | frames counted by channel i | - |
| 0x50 | TIME | RO | 0 | timestamp now (ticks of TS_DIV clocks) | - |
| 0x54 | EV_EN | RW | 0 | channels logged in the event log | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/video/frame_counter/src/include/frame_counter_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 366 LUTs, 508 flip-flops. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for frame_counter (NCH = 3, EVQ = 8,
TS_DIV = 3). A reference model (counts, STATUS, event log) follows every
marker pulse and register write; the tests compare the DUT's COUNT[i],
STATUS, irq_o and logged events with it: register reset values,
the ID block, counting, interrupt enable and write-1-to-clear, CLEAR, a marker in the
same clock as a clear, a random mix of all of them, the timestamp
divider, the event log order (also for markers in one clock and in
consecutive clocks), a full log (overflow) and disabled channels.
Prints TEST PASSED on success; +vcd dumps
frame_counter_tb.vcd. The test tasks are in tests/frame_counter_tests.sv
(`included).
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh frame_counter --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_registers` | reset values of IRQ_EN, STATUS, EVENT, EV_EN and every COUNT |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_count` | Pulses on single channels and on several at once are counted per channel |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_irq` | irq_o = STATUS & IRQ_EN per channel; STATUS stays set until written with 1 (write 0 keeps it) |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_clear` | CLEAR zeroes only the channels written with 1 |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_clear_collision` | An end of frame in the clock of a CLEAR counts (the count becomes 1) and one in the clock of a STATUS clear keeps STATUS set |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_random` | 2000 clocks of random pulses with random CLEAR, STATUS and IRQ_EN writes, checked against the model after every register access |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_time` | TIME advances by one every TS_DIV clocks |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_event_order` | Markers on every channel, apart and interleaved: logged in marker order with the channel's count and the timestamp of the marker; reading EVENT does not remove it, EVENT_POP does |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_event_same_clock` | Markers of several channels in one clock and a lower channel in the next clock: one timestamp, lowest channel first, the later marker after them |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_event_overflow` | More markers than the log holds: the first EVQ kept in order, EVENT[30] set until EVENT_POP[1] |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_event_disabled` | A channel not enabled in EV_EN is counted but not logged |
| `frame_counter_tb` | `test_id_block` | ID, VERSION ("d.dd") and DATE (BCD mm/dd/yyyy) at the base address, read only; the map after them at 0x10 |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |

| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
